[1] customer-service-playbook.md > Goodwill and approvals
## Repairs

Any repair, under warranty or paid, gets a repair ticket in the form RT-xxxxx (five digits), for
example RT-20931. Create it in the Hearth admin from the warranty claim or from scratch for a paid
repair. The ticket number goes on the box and in the email to the customer.

Customers can drop a lantern off at either showroom or mail it to Lantern Supply Co. Repair
Center, 1180 Downsville Pike, Dock B, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Annapolis drop-offs are shipped to
Hagerstown weekly on Tuesdays, so tell Annapolis customers to add a week. Walt Brannigan, Head
of Repairs, emails a quote for paid repairs before any work is done; nothing is charged until the
customer approves the quote. Fuel lanterns must be emptied before they are mailed; tell the
customer, and put it in the email.

## Goodwill and approvals

You may give a goodwill credit of up to $25 per incident without approval: a discount code, a
free mantle pack, a refunded shipping charge. Log it on the ticket with a one-line reason.

Above $25, ask the shift lead. The Three Lights rule covers larger amounts: any refund, credit or
goodwill over $500 needs the approval of Tomas Reyes, and anything over $2,000 needs the approval
of Priya Whitcomb-Nair. "Any" means any: a refund that is simply the price of a returned Sentinel
1000 Pro and a Northstar together is over $500 and needs Tomas's sign-off before it is released,
even though the policy clearly allows it. Approvals are recorded on the ticket as a note from the
approver, not as a verbal okay.

## Escalation path

Agent, then shift lead, then Tomas Reyes. Escalate when a customer asks for a manager twice, when
a decision needs an approval you cannot give, when a customer mentions a lawyer, a regulator or
the press, or when you are not sure. Hand the ticket over with a two-line summary at the top: what
happened, what the customer wants. Do not promise a callback time for someone else; say that the
shift lead will be in touch by the end of the next business day.

Safety reports, meaning any claim that a product caught fire, leaked fuel, overheated or injured
someone, go to Tomas Reyes and Walt Brannigan the same day, whatever the amount, and the product is
recalled to Hagerstown for inspection at our expense.

[2] returns-policy.md > Approvals: the Three Lights rule
## Holiday extension

Orders delivered between November 1 and December 24 may be returned until January 31 of the
following year. All other terms of this policy still apply: the item must be unused, in its
packaging, not final sale, and fuel-free. The extension applies automatically in Hearth; agents do
not need to adjust the window by hand.

## Approvals: the Three Lights rule

Any refund, credit or goodwill gesture over $500 on a single order needs the approval of Tomas
Reyes before it is issued. Anything over $2,000 needs the approval of Priya Whitcomb-Nair. Agents
may issue goodwill credits of up to $25 per incident on their own authority. The approval is
recorded as a note on the order in Hearth with the approver's name and the date. The rule takes
its name from the three lights on the old warehouse sign and is explained in full in the Customer
Service Playbook.

## Common situations

A customer wants to return a lantern after 40 days. The answer is no, unless the holiday extension
applies. Agents may offer to check the item under warranty if there is a defect.

A customer bought a Firefly 220R (LS-220R) and meant to buy the Firefly 220 (LS-220). This is a
simple exchange; no restocking fee, and the replacement ships at once because the price
difference is under $50.

A customer has lit their new Northstar once in the backyard and does not like the sound of the
pressurized tank. The item cannot be returned; fuel has been put in it. The agent should explain
why and note that the warranty still covers any defect.

A customer's return arrived at the warehouse damaged in transit without insurance. The warehouse
photographs the damage and customer service offers a partial refund at the shift lead's
discretion; the customer is responsible for a return package until it arrives.

[3] employee-handbook.md > Employee discount
### Other benefits

Full-time employees receive a company-paid life insurance policy of $25,000, a pretax commuter
benefit of up to $150 a month, and an annual stipend of $200 for work boots or safety footwear for
warehouse and repair staff. The company pays for the ServSafe-style fuel handling certification
required for warehouse staff and renews it every three years.

## Employee discount

Every employee, full-time or part-time, gets 30% off the retail price of anything we sell, in the
showrooms or on the online store, and 50% off Second Light refurbished items. The discount applies
to merchandise, not to shipping, repairs or gift cards. Employees may spend up to $2,000 a year at
the discounted price; purchases past the cap are at retail. The cap resets on January 1.

The discount is for you and the people in your household. Buying discounted items to resell, or
for friends outside your household, is a conduct violation and ends the discount. Use the
discount code on your employee ID card online, or give your employee number at the register. Your
discounted purchases still earn Lumen Rewards points on the amount you actually paid.

## Dress code

Showroom and support staff wear the lantern green polo (we provide three) with your name tag,
with dark trousers, jeans without holes, or a knee-length skirt, and closed-toe shoes. Warehouse
and repair staff wear the grey Lantern Supply Co. work shirt, long trousers and steel-toe or
composite-toe boots; the boot stipend above covers them. Hats are fine in the warehouse, not in
the showrooms. Replacement polos and name tags come from Beth Carrow; a replacement name tag
takes about a week.

[4] employee-handbook.md > Customer service standards
Demonstration lanterns on the floor run on Clearburn white gas or lamp oil as the product
requires. Never fuel a demonstration lantern on the sales floor; take it to the back-room fueling
tray. Never fuel a hot lantern; let it cool for 10 minutes. Spills are cleaned at once with the
absorbent pads in the cabinet, and the pads go in the red bin, not the trash.

Fire extinguishers at every location are checked monthly by Denise Okafor, the Warehouse
Manager, or by a person she designates in writing, and the check is recorded on the tag. If a tag
is more than 31 days old, tell your manager that day. Every employee is shown how to use an
extinguisher in their first week. A showroom never has fewer than two working extinguishers on
the floor.

Fuel sold in a showroom goes out in the customer's hands; we never ship fuel from a showroom.
Fuel ordered online ships by ground only from Hagerstown, never to a PO box and never to Alaska,
Hawaii or Canada. If a customer asks you to make an exception, the answer is no.

## Customer service standards

Every email to help@lanternsupply.example is answered within 1 business day, and most are answered
the same day. A phone caller should wait less than 3 minutes; if the queue is longer than that,
the shift lead pulls in a second person. Chat on the online store follows the same 3-minute
standard during support hours and shows the next-day email promise outside them.

Know the policies before you quote them. The return window is 40 days from the delivery date,
the standard warranty is 2 years, and the full details are in the returns policy, the shipping
policy, the warranty policy and the customer service playbook. Any refund, credit or goodwill over
$500 needs approval from Tomas Reyes, Head of Customer Service, and anything over $2,000 needs
Priya Whitcomb-Nair's. Do not promise what you cannot approve.

## Breaks and meal periods

Anyone working more than 6 consecutive hours takes an unpaid meal break of at least 30 minutes,
as Maryland's Healthy Retail Employee Act requires for retail staff, and a paid 15-minute break
for every 4 hours worked. Showroom breaks are staggered so that at least two people are on the
floor at all times; the shift lead sets the order each morning. Meal breaks are clocked out in
Deputy. Warehouse breaks follow the bell at 9:30 AM, noon and 2:15 PM. Nobody eats at the repair
bench or near the fuel cabinet.

[5] returns-policy.md > Refunds
## Return authorization numbers

Every mailed return needs a return authorization number before it ships. RA numbers have the form
RA- followed by six digits, for example RA-118204. The number is printed on the packing slip
that comes with the prepaid label and must also be written on the outside of the box.

Customers obtain an RA number by:

- Using "Start a return" on the online store, which issues the number immediately for any
  eligible order and emails it with a packing slip.
- Calling (301) 555-0147 during support hours. The agent creates the return in Hearth and reads
  the number back.

A package that arrives at the warehouse without an RA number is held for 10 business days while
the warehouse tries to match it to an order. If it cannot be matched it is returned to the sender
at the sender's cost. The RA number is valid for 30 days from issue.

## Refunds

Refunds go to the original payment method. The warehouse inspects each return within 2 business
days of arrival and the refund is issued within 7 business days of the return arriving at the
Hagerstown warehouse. Card refunds typically appear on the customer's statement 3 to 5 business
days after they are issued; this is the card issuer's timing and the company cannot speed it up.

The refund covers the item price paid, less any restocking fee and less the $8.50 prepaid label
fee if one was used. Original outbound shipping charges are refunded only when the item was
defective or the wrong item was shipped.

If the original payment method is a card that has since been closed, the refund is issued as a
store credit to the customer's Lumen Rewards account, or as a check mailed within 14 business
days if the customer has no account.

Gift recipients returning an item without the original payment details receive store credit for
the item's price on the gift receipt.

## In-store returns

Both showrooms accept returns of items bought online, by phone, or in either showroom. The
customer should bring the packing slip or the order number and the payment card used. Showroom
staff process the return in Hearth on the spot; the refund timing is the same 7 business days.
Items returned in store are held in the showroom's returns cage and shipped to Hagerstown on the
weekly Tuesday transfer.

Showrooms may accept unopened fuel and unopened consumables, which cannot be mailed. Showrooms do
not accept items that have had fuel put in them, for the same reason the warehouse does not.
